user.title: ROS 2 Bridge
user.description: The bridge rides Home Assistant's own MQTT connection, so the broker is already known. Choose the topic prefix the robots publish under and, if the robots require signed commands, the shared secret configured on them.

data_description.topic_prefix: The first part of every bridge topic (prefix, then the robot id, then the message kind). No leading or trailing slash, no wildcards, not the MQTT discovery prefix. Must match the prefix configured on the robots.
data_description.shared_secret: Optional. When set, every command is signed with HMAC-SHA256 and the robots refuse unsigned commands. Leave empty to send unsigned commands.

confirm.title: Robot found
confirm.description: Found robot {robot_name} announcing under the topic prefix {topic_prefix}. Create the ROS 2 Bridge entry?

data_description.shared_secret: Optional. The shared secret configured on the robots, when they require signed commands.

error.invalid_prefix: The topic prefix must not be empty, contain + or #, start or end with a slash, be the MQTT discovery prefix (homeassistant) or start with the reserved segment ha.

abort.already_configured: The ROS 2 Bridge is already configured.
abort.single_instance_allowed: Already configured. Only a single configuration is possible.
abort.mqtt_not_configured: The MQTT integration is not configured. Set up MQTT first; the bridge uses its connection.
abort.mqtt_not_available: The MQTT client did not become available. Check the MQTT integration and try again.
abort.invalid_discovery_info: The discovered message is not a valid robot announce.

init.title: ROS 2 Bridge options

data_description.topic_prefix: Changing the prefix moves every subscription and publication; the robots must be configured with the same prefix.
data_description.shared_secret: Leave empty to send unsigned commands. When set, it must match the secret configured on the robots.
data_description.heartbeat_interval_s: How often Home Assistant publishes its heartbeat to the robots, in seconds. 0 disables it; robots then report the link as down.
data_description.ack_timeout_s: How long to wait for a robot to acknowledge a command before it is reported as not acknowledged (outcome unknown).
data_description.command_max_age_ms: How long a command stays valid after it is issued, in milliseconds. Robots refuse older commands as stale, and each node clamps the value to its own command.max_age_cap_ms (default 30000).
data_description.result_timeout_margin_s: Extra seconds beyond a task's announced timeout before Home Assistant reports a missing result.
data_description.max_pending_per_robot: How many commands may be outstanding per robot at once; further commands are refused.
data_description.heartbeat_unavailable_after_s: Seconds without a robot heartbeat before its entities become unavailable. 0 disables this. Keep it above the stale threshold (Advanced: heartbeat stale intervals, times the robot's heartbeat interval), or the entities go unavailable before the problem sensor can warn.
data_description.mirror_entities: Entities republished to the robots under the prefix's ha/sensors topics in the canonical sensor schema, one retained message per entity, on every state or attribute change.
data_description.intent_ack_wait_s: How long a voice command waits for the robot's acknowledgement before replying "I will report back", in seconds. Never longer than the acknowledgement timeout.
data_description.joint_moving_threshold: A joint sensor's moving attribute turns on when the robot's reported velocity exceeds this, in the announced unit per second; a robot that reports no velocities is judged by its positions instead, moving when one changed by more than this since the previous report. Reported velocities decide alone, so a reported 0 means at rest even if the position still changed. 0 uses the unit's default: 0.5 for degrees, 0.01 for radians.
data_description.joint_moving_hold_s: How long a report's moving verdict stands when no newer report arrives, in seconds, after which the joint counts as still. A robot publishes positions only when they change, so a slowly moving joint reports less often than its announced rate; raise this if moving flickers during a slow sweep. 0 means two publication intervals of the robot's announced rate, never less than 1 s.
data_description.mirror_extra_attributes: Attribute names added to the built-in allowlist of attributes a mirrored entity may carry to the robots, one name per entry (for example pm2_5 or moisture). Everything published here is readable by every client of the broker: never add locations, tokens, identifiers or anything else private.

init.description: Everyday settings are on this form. The timings shared with the robot nodes and the heuristics behind two repairs are under Advanced; their defaults match the nodes' defaults, so change them only together with the matching node parameter.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Timings the robot nodes share and the heuristics behind two repairs. The defaults are the nodes' defaults; an expiry changed here must be changed on every node too.

data_description.ack_expiry_s: Must equal the nodes' reply.ack_expiry_s: how long a retained acknowledgement lives on the broker, in seconds. It is how long a cancel waits for its acknowledgement.
data_description.result_expiry_s: Must equal the nodes' reply.result_expiry_s: how long a retained result lives on the broker, in seconds. Home Assistant remembers seen result ids for this long plus the result timeout margin, so a retained replay after a restart never fires a task result twice.
data_description.replay_settle_s: Quiet period after the subscriptions are confirmed and MQTT is connected before outstanding commands are reconciled against the retained replay, in seconds. A large fleet or a slow broker may want longer.
data_description.session_change_grace_s: How long after a robot's session changes (its node restarted) Home Assistant waits for that robot's retained results before marking its outstanding commands lost, in seconds.
data_description.feedback_throttle_ms: The least time between two feedback writes (progress, stage, message) into a robot's state sensor, in milliseconds; 0 writes every feedback. Set it to 1000 divided by the nodes' reply.feedback_max_rate_hz to show every message.
data_description.heartbeat_stale_intervals: How many of the robot's announced heartbeat intervals may pass without a heartbeat before it counts as stale (problem sensor reason heartbeat_stale). Raise it on a jittery network.
data_description.clock_skew_warn_ms: An acknowledgement reporting a clock difference of this many milliseconds or more opens the clock skew repair. Keep it below the nodes' command.clock_skew_tolerance_ms (default 2000).
data_description.duplicate_session_changes: More than this many session changes of one robot within the window below open the duplicate robot id repair.
data_description.duplicate_session_window_s: The sliding window the session changes are counted over, in seconds. It also bounds how long a second instance's heartbeats are remembered.
data_description.duplicate_quiet_s: Seconds without new evidence after which the duplicate robot id repair closes by itself.

error.invalid_prefix: The topic prefix must not be empty, contain + or #, start or end with a slash, be the MQTT discovery prefix (homeassistant) or start with the reserved segment ha.

send_task.name: Send task
send_task.description: Sends a task command to one or more robots and optionally waits for the acknowledgement or the result.

device_id.name: Robot device
device_id.description: The robot device or devices to send the task to.

robot_id.name: Robot ID
robot_id.description: The robot's id as announced on the broker, as an alternative to a device.

task.name: Task
task.description: The announced task name, for example reset or move_to.

params.name: Parameters
params.description: Parameters for the task, matching the schema the robot announced for it.

wait.name: Wait for
wait.description: Return after the acknowledgement (default), after the result, or at once.

timeout_s.name: Timeout
timeout_s.description: Overrides the task's announced timeout, in seconds. The robot may clamp it.

max_age_ms.name: Maximum age
max_age_ms.description: Overrides the command maximum age option for this command, in milliseconds.

cancel_task.name: Cancel task
cancel_task.description: Cancels the running task of one or more robots, or one task by its id.

device_id.name: Robot device
device_id.description: The robot device or devices whose task to cancel.

robot_id.name: Robot ID
robot_id.description: The robot's id as announced on the broker, as an alternative to a device.

task_id.name: Task ID
task_id.description: The id of the task to cancel. Leave empty to cancel the robot's active motion task.

wait.name: Wait for
wait.description: Return after the cancel is acknowledged (default), after the cancelled task's result, or at once.

max_age_ms.name: Maximum age
max_age_ms.description: Overrides the command maximum age option for this cancel, in milliseconds.

get_robots.name: Get robots
get_robots.description: Returns every announced robot with its availability, state and task catalogue.

not_loaded.message: The ROS 2 Bridge is not loaded.

not_ready.message: The ROS 2 Bridge is not ready yet: its MQTT subscriptions have not been confirmed.

robot_unknown.message: Robot {robot_id} is not known; it has not announced itself on the broker.

task_unknown.message: Robot {robot_id} does not announce a task called {task}.

invalid_params.message: The parameters for task {task} on robot {robot_id} are invalid: {problems}.

publish_failed.message: The command for robot {robot_id} could not be published: {error}. It stays tracked; if the connection returns before the acknowledgement timeout the message is delivered, otherwise the command is reported as not acknowledged (outcome unknown).

no_ack.message: Robot {robot_id} did not acknowledge the command in time; the outcome is unknown.

no_result.message: Robot {robot_id} did not report a result for task {task} before the deadline.

clock_skew.title: Clock skew with robot {robot_id}
clock_skew.description: Robot {robot_id} reports a clock difference of {skew_ms} ms against Home Assistant. Commands carry an issue time and a maximum age, so a difference above the robot's tolerance makes it refuse them as stale or from the future. Check that both machines use NTP and that their clocks agree to within two seconds. The threshold is the clock skew warning option under Advanced. This issue closes by itself once an acknowledgement arrives with an acceptable difference.

hmac_rejected.title: Robot {robot_id} refused the command signature
hmac_rejected.description: Robot {robot_id} rejected a command as unauthorised: {reason}. Make sure the shared secret in the ROS 2 Bridge options matches the secret configured on the robot, or clear it on both sides to send unsigned commands. This issue closes by itself once the robot accepts a command.

invalid_announce.title: Robot {robot_id} sent an invalid announce
invalid_announce.description: The retained message on {topic} is not a valid announce: {reason}. The robot is not shown until it announces correctly. Check the robot's bridge version and its task catalogue, then restart the robot node. This issue closes by itself once a valid announce arrives.

mqtt_v5_required.title: The MQTT connection does not support message expiry
mqtt_v5_required.description: Publishing to {topic} with a message expiry interval was refused because Home Assistant's MQTT session is not MQTT 5. Commands were sent without an expiry, so a stale command can sit in the broker until a robot reads it; the robots still refuse commands older than their maximum age. Set the MQTT integration's protocol to 5 and make sure the broker supports it. This issue closes by itself once a publish with an expiry succeeds.

duplicate_robot_id.title: Two robot nodes may be using the id {robot_id}
duplicate_robot_id.description: Home Assistant saw evidence that more than one bridge node is publishing as robot {robot_id}: {detail}. Two nodes with one id take each other's broker session over in turn and their state, acknowledgements and results interleave. A node that crashes and restarts repeatedly can trip this check too, which also needs attention. Give each robot its own robot.id parameter and restart the nodes. This issue closes by itself after {quiet_minutes} quiet minutes (the duplicate robot id quiet period option).
